concepts.name: Constitutional Basis of the Budget: Article 112 and Annual Financial Statement
key_dimensions: Article 112 mandates the Annual Financial Statement (AFS); 'Budget' is nowhere mentioned in the Constitution
Distinction between AFS, Budget, and Finance Bill — UPSC trap on terminology
Three-part division of AFS: Consolidated Fund, Contingency Fund, Public Account
Comparison with State budget under Article 202

concepts.name: Consolidated Fund of India vs. Contingency Fund vs. Public Account
key_dimensions: Constitutional provisions: Articles 266, 267 — sources, withdrawals, and authorization requirements
Consolidated Fund requires Parliamentary approval; Public Account does not require Parliamentary vote
Contingency Fund operates as an imprest — size, authorization, and recoupment process
UPSC trap: Which fund does NOT require Parliamentary approval for withdrawal

concepts.name: Presentation of the Budget: Timing, Authority, and Recent Reforms
key_dimensions: Constitutional provision: No fixed date in Constitution; convention of last day of February changed to February 1 (since 2017)
Abolition of Railway Budget (merged with Union Budget from 2017) — Acworth Committee origin
Who presents: Finance Minister; in absence, PM or any minister authorized
Advance presentation rationale: full budget operation from April 1, avoiding Vote on Account dependency

concepts.name: Stages of Budget Passage in Parliament: The Six-Stage Process
key_dimensions: Six stages: Presentation → General Discussion → Scrutiny by DRSCs → Voting on Demands for Grants → Appropriation Bill → Finance Bill
UPSC trap: Rajya Sabha's role — cannot vote on Demands for Grants; can only discuss
General discussion: No voting, no referral to committee at this stage
Distinction between stages applicable to Money Bill vs. ordinary budget stages

concepts.name: Demands for Grants: Nature, Types, and Voting Rules
key_dimensions: Only Lok Sabha votes on Demands for Grants — Article 113; Rajya Sabha has no power to amend or reject
Three types of cuts: Policy Cut, Economy Cut, Token Cut — purpose and implication of each
Charged expenditure vs. voted expenditure — what can and cannot be voted upon
Guillotine: Time-limit mechanism where undiscussed demands are put to vote automatically

concepts.name: Charged Expenditure: Constitutional Provisions and Significance
key_dimensions: Article 112(3): Items charged on Consolidated Fund — not subject to vote of Parliament
List of charged items: President's salary, Supreme Court judges, CAG, Speaker, debt charges, etc.
UPSC trap: Can Parliament discuss but not vote on charged expenditure
Rationale: Insulating constitutional functionaries from political pressures of annual voting

concepts.name: Appropriation Bill: Purpose, Constitutional Basis, and Restrictions
key_dimensions: Article 114: No money can be withdrawn from Consolidated Fund without Appropriation Act
Appropriation Bill cannot be amended to vary the amount or alter the destination of grants
Rajya Sabha's role: Can recommend amendments but Lok Sabha not bound to accept — Money Bill provisions apply
UPSC trap: Appropriation Bill vs. Finance Bill — which is a Money Bill, which amends tax law

concepts.name: Finance Bill: Classification, Types, and Constitutional Provisions
key_dimensions: Finance Bill Type 1 (Article 110): Contains only Money Bill matters — Rajya Sabha can only recommend
Finance Bill Type 2 (Article 117): Contains some Money Bill and other matters — joint sitting possible
Finance Bill vs. Money Bill — UPSC trap: Not all Finance Bills are Money Bills
Finance Bill must be passed within 75 days; implications if not passed

concepts.name: Vote on Account: Purpose, Duration, and Distinction from Full Budget
key_dimensions: Article 116(1)(a): Allows government to meet expenditure before full budget is passed
Convention: 1/6th of total estimated expenditure for 2 months (election year: up to 4 months)
UPSC trap: Vote on Account is only for expenditure, not for taxation changes
Distinction from Interim Budget: Interim Budget includes both receipts and expenditure; Vote on Account only expenditure

concepts.name: Interim Budget vs. Vote on Account: Differences and Constitutional Position
key_dimensions: 'Interim Budget' has no constitutional basis — purely a political/executive convention
Vote on Account has constitutional backing under Article 116; Interim Budget does not
UPSC trap: An Interim Budget can present tax changes; Vote on Account cannot
Historical context: 2019 Interim Budget included direct tax relief — controversy around convention violation

concepts.name: Supplementary, Additional, and Excess Grants: Article 115 and 116
key_dimensions: Article 115: Three situations — new service not contemplated, excess over authorized amount, supplementary sum
Excess Grant: Article 115(1)(b) — requires CAG report and PAC recommendation before Lok Sabha votes
UPSC trap: Excess Grant is for past expenditure; Supplementary is for future anticipated excess
Token Grant and Exceptional Grant as sub-types — purpose and procedural nuances

concepts.name: Role of Rajya Sabha in Budget: Powers, Limitations, and 14-Day Rule
key_dimensions: Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject Demands for Grants or Appropriation Bill — Article 109
Finance Bill (if Money Bill): Rajya Sabha can only recommend; Lok Sabha not bound — Article 110
14-day rule: If Rajya Sabha does not return Money Bill in 14 days, deemed passed by both Houses
UPSC trap: Rajya Sabha CAN discuss the budget but has no voting power on grants

concepts.name: Departmentally Related Standing Committees (DRSCs) and Budget Scrutiny
key_dimensions: 24 DRSCs examine Demands for Grants of respective ministries and submit reports
Reports are recommendatory — Parliament is not bound to accept their recommendations
UPSC trap: DRSCs examine demands BEFORE voting, not after; unlike PAC which is post-facto
Composition: Members from both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha — joint committees

concepts.name: Public Accounts Committee (PAC): Role in Budget Accountability
key_dimensions: Post-budget scrutiny body — examines CAG audit reports on actual expenditure vs. appropriation
Composition: 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS); chaired by Leader of Opposition (convention since 1967)
UPSC trap: PAC cannot question policy; can only examine whether money was spent as Parliament intended
Distinction from Estimates Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings

concepts.name: Estimates Committee: Composition, Role, and Distinction from PAC
key_dimensions: Largest Parliamentary committee: 30 members, all from Lok Sabha only (Rajya Sabha excluded)
Examines estimates BEFORE they are voted — suggests economies and alternative policies
UPSC trap: Estimates Committee can suggest policy alternatives; PAC cannot
Cannot question the policies approved by Parliament — only examines how those policies are implemented economically

concepts.name: Guillotine in Budget Voting: Mechanism and Constitutional Implications
key_dimensions: Time allocation for budget discussion is limited; undiscussed demands are automatically put to vote at the end
Guillotine is a procedural device — not mentioned in Constitution but in Rules of Procedure
UPSC angle: Undermines detailed parliamentary scrutiny — democratic accountability concern
Typically, only a fraction of demands are actually discussed before guillotine is applied

concepts.name: Cut Motions: Policy Cut, Economy Cut, and Token Cut — Procedure and Significance
key_dimensions: Policy Cut: Reduce demand to Re.1 — disapproves the policy underlying the demand
Economy Cut: Reduce by a specified amount — suggests economy in expenditure
Token Cut: Reduce by Rs.100 — used to ventilate a specific grievance; not to reduce overall spending
UPSC trap: Cut motions are moved in Lok Sabha only; if passed, government faces confidence vote implications

concepts.name: Zero-Based Budgeting vs. Traditional/Incremental Budgeting: Concepts and Indian Context
key_dimensions: Traditional budgeting: Previous year's allocation + increment; ZBB: Every scheme justified from scratch each year
India introduced ZBB in 1986 for plan expenditure; not consistently followed
Outcome-based budgeting and Performance Budget as related modern concepts
UPSC angle: ZBB reduces incremental bias but increases administrative burden — trade-offs

concepts.name: FRBM Act 2003: Fiscal Deficit Targets, Escape Clauses, and Budget Discipline
key_dimensions: FRBM mandates reducing fiscal deficit; targets revised multiple times — current medium-term target 4.5% by 2025-26
Escape clause (Section 4(2)): Government can deviate by 0.5% of GDP in case of national security, calamity, or structural reforms
N.K. Singh Committee (2017): Recommended fiscal council, debt-to-GDP target of 60% (40% Centre + 20% States)
UPSC trap: FRBM is a statutory constraint on budget, not a Constitutional one — can be amended by simple legislation

concepts.name: Budget and Secrecy Convention: Halwa Ceremony, Lockdown, and Constitutional Basis
key_dimensions: Budget secrecy is a constitutional convention, not a Constitutional provision — based on Article 112 read with parliamentary privileges
Budget documents are prepared under lockdown in North Block to prevent pre-budget leaks
Halwa ceremony marks beginning of printing; no official outside until budget is presented
UPSC trap: Budget secrecy convention was breached in 1950 (Krishnamachari) and 1987 (Chidambaram) — consequences
